statement: The Kronecker delta is a function of two variables (usually non-negative integers), or a tensor, defined by \delta_j^i = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } i = j \\ 0 & \text{if } i \neq j \end{cases}

symbols.meaning: Kronecker delta function or tensor component

properties.property: Represents the identity mapping (or identity matrix) considered as a linear mapping V \to V or V^* \to V^*
properties.why: acts identically on vectors or dual vectors

properties.property: Represents the trace or tensor contraction considered as a mapping V^* \otimes V \to K
properties.why: evaluates tensor contraction between dual vectors and vectors

properties.property: Represents the map K \to V^* \otimes V representing scalar multiplication as a sum of outer products
properties.why: maps field scalars into the tensor product space

properties.property: Contour and trigonometric integral representation: \delta_{jk} = \frac{1}{2\pi i} \oint_{|z|=1} z^{j-k-1}\,dz = \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} e^{i(j-k)\varphi}\,d\varphi for integers j, k
properties.why: evaluates residue on the counterclockwise unit circle in the complex plane
summing repeated indices over the d-dimensional space

assumptions.assumption: Indices or variables are discrete (usually non-negative integers)
assumptions.breaks_when: Applied over continuous domains where the Dirac delta distribution is required instead

failure_modes.signature: Expressions differ by factors of p!
failure_modes.cause: Two conventions are in use for the generalized Kronecker delta differing by a factor of p!

failure_modes.signature: Contraction gives incorrect scalar or tensor magnitude
failure_modes.cause: Contractions of generalized Kronecker deltas explicitly depend on the dimension d of the space
